title: RULES ON THE REMUNERATION OF JUDGES
full_text:
RULES ON THE REMUNERATION OF JUDGES

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe judges' salaries and other remuneration, the methods of paying remuneration, the calculation of remuneration, and other matters necessary for implementing the Remuneration of Judges Act pursuant to the proviso to Article 2 and Article 6 of that Act.

Article 2 (Standards for Remuneration)
Judges shall receive salaries based on Annex 1 and other remuneration. <Amended on April 8, 1996; August 18, 2000; May 1, 2007>

Article 3 (Salary Adjustment Allowance)
(1) A salary adjustment allowance may be paid within the budget when necessary to improve the treatment of judges. <Amended on May 1, 2007>
(2) The salary adjustment allowance shall be paid under item 1 of Annex 2.
(3) On January 1 of each year, the amount calculated under item 2 of Annex 2 shall be incorporated into the salary amount.

Article 4 (Prohibition of Withholding and Similar Deductions)
(1) An agency paying remuneration shall not regularly withhold, specially collect or deduct a specified amount from remuneration (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "withholding and similar deductions"), except in any of the following cases: <Amended on May 25, 2017; March 5, 2019>
1. Where withholding and similar deductions are required by statutes or regulations;
2. Where withholding and similar deductions are made for contributions and similar payments to a mutual aid association established by law;
3. Where withholding and similar deductions are required by a court ruling;
4. Where withholding and similar deductions concern matters to which the person concerned has consented, for a period selected by that person, by submitting a written document or through an electronic personnel management system (a system that maintains personnel records in a database and enables electronic processing of personnel affairs) to a disbursing officer under Article 2, subparagraph 1 (a), of the Act on the Liability of Accounting Officials, etc. (excluding acting disbursing officers, sub-disbursing officers and acting sub-disbursing officers).
(2) The Minister of National Court Administration shall determine the methods, operation and other matters necessary for withholding and similar deductions under paragraph (1).

Article 5 (Methods of Paying Remuneration)
(1) Remuneration shall be paid in cash or by demand deposit, except where otherwise specifically prescribed by statutes or regulations.
(2) Remuneration shall be paid directly to the person concerned. However, where direct payment is impossible owing to a business trip or another unavoidable reason, it may be paid to a person designated by that person.

Article 6 (Calculation of Remuneration)
Except where otherwise specifically prescribed by statutes or regulations, judges' remuneration shall be paid by prorating the monthly amount on a daily basis by reference to the date of the personnel order in all cases, including appointment, transfer, advancement in salary step and salary reduction.

Article 7 (Payment of Salary upon Separation from Office during a Month, etc. of Judges with at Least Five Years of Continuous Service)
In any of the following cases, notwithstanding Article 6, the full salary for the month in which the date of separation from office or commencement of leave falls shall be paid:
1. Where a judge with at least five years of continuous service leaves office during a month after working for at least 15 days in that month. This excludes removal from office by an impeachment decision or by a sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment;
2. Where a judge with at least two years of continuous service takes leave to perform an obligation under the Military Service Act or another law;
3. Where a judge dies while in office in the course of official duties, or dies while in office from a duty-related illness or injury, and is consequently separated from office (excluding separation dated the first day of that month).

ADDENDUM — Supreme Court Rule No. 2320, January 31, 2011
Article 1 (Enforcement Date)

Article 2 (Special Cases concerning the Basis for Calculating Monthly Salary, etc. for Honorary Retirement Allowances)
(1) The monthly salary forming the basis for calculating the honorary retirement allowances of judges and court officials under the Rules on Payment of Honorary Retirement Allowances, etc. to Judges and Court Officials shall be calculated on the basis of 68 percent of the salary amount in the applicable salary table.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for officials subject to the performance-related annual salary system, the monthly salary forming the basis for calculating the honorary retirement allowance under the Rules on Payment of Honorary Retirement Allowances, etc. to Judges and Court Officials shall be calculated on the basis of 81 percent of 66 percent of the monthly amount of annual salary (meaning the amount excluding the performance-related annual salary component).

Item 3 in the notes to Annex 1 shall read as follows:
3. They shall also apply to the calculation of early retirement allowances and voluntary retirement allowances under Article 10 (3) of these Rules.
(a) For officials subject to the salary-step system, monthly salary shall be 68 percent of the salary amount in the salary table.
(b) For officials subject to the performance-related annual salary system, monthly salary shall be 81 percent of 66 percent of the monthly amount of annual salary (meaning the amount excluding the performance-related annual salary component).
